source.title: One coordinate breaks abliteration on Gemma-3

record.tranche_reason: Applies difference-in-means refusal-direction extraction and projection-based ablation, and reports refusal and capability outcomes across models. It also tests additive steering with extracted directions.
record.gate_note: The post reports values for clean, raw, corrected, per-layer, and random-direction conditions. The feasibility counts are selection/filter outcomes rather than refusal-rate results, so they are not cataloged as rows. The reported degeneration column is omitted to prioritize refusal and MMLU outcomes. Related-work results are not included.
record.test_reason: Applies the original recipe to Gemma-3-12B, Llama-3-8B and Qwen-2.5-7B: harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means at t_post_inst, the Arditi feasibility filter, projection ablation and additive induction. It reports refusal, degeneration and MMLU against clean and random-direction controls. It also shows the raw estimator fails on Gemma-3 and that scale-corrected variants work.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that a dominant-scale coordinate in Gemma-3 corrupts raw difference-in-means estimation and projection. Scale corrections (masking, standardization, winsorization) restore ablation that suppresses refusal while matching clean MMLU, so difficulty of removal is not evidence of inseparability from capability. They recommend channel-standardized difference-in-means and explicitly decline to claim a universal one-dimensional refusal representation or to refute multidimensional accounts.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful-minus-harmless mean activation differences and projection-based ablation, with a feasibility filter and selected source layer/token position; ablation applies the selected direction at stated sites. Adds masking, channel standardization, and winsorization to address a dominant coordinate. Also reports additive steering. It does not establish exact equivalence to the original procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Strong dependence on model family and direction recipe: raw extraction has no feasible candidate for Gemma-3-12B, while scale-corrected recipes yield candidates; raw directions work on Llama-3-8B and Qwen-2.5-7B. Alternative prompt contrasts show residual refusal. The post also varies layer-specific versus reused directions and reports that length matching and covariate adjustment do not recover feasible Gemma-3-12B candidates.

fits_no_version.finding: Class separation in the standardized difference vector is diffuse (top-1000 coordinates hold 72–75% of energy). Probes reach ~0.9 AUROC with or without the loud coordinate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful/harmless separation in Gemma-3-12B is spread across many coordinates despite one dominant-scale channel.

fits_no_version.finding: Zeroing the loud channel, or a leak-only intervention, drops MMLU to near chance across Gemma-3 sizes. Llama and Qwen are barely affected.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A single massive-activation channel in Gemma-3 is necessary for capability and corrupts raw difference-in-means estimation and projection.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the behavioral or capability results. Main prompt contrast uses AdvBench and SORRY-Bench versus Alpaca; the post notes results for a limited set of 32 prompts for additive steering. Raw Gemma-3-12B direction has no feasible cell under the selection filter, so it is not directly comparable to selected feasible directions. The capability assessment is a roughly 500-question MMLU slice supplemented by NLL; broad preservation of other abilities is not established.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted degeneration-rate cells from the main three-model recipe table to prioritize refusal and MMLU measures. Also omitted the feasibility-count tables and the per-model loud-channel profile tables: these concern candidate filtering or activation-scale diagnosis rather than refusal-rate or capability outcomes for the refusal-direction intervention.

untested.parts: Abilities beyond a 500-question MMLU slice and NLL; models beyond 7–12B in the behavioural table (larger Gemma-3 sizes have only feasibility and KL results).
No weight-space edit or released abliterated model is evaluated; all interventions are at inference time.
No causal comparison of affine, cone or multi-direction accounts; the authors explicitly do not address this.
No cross-language or base-to-instruct transfer of the direction; the base checkpoint is examined only for the loud channel.
The loud channel predates instruction tuning, but the post does not test how training creates a refusal direction.

missing.what: Llama-3-8B refusal under the two alternative contrasts does not drop below 0.36 and 0.69 (clean baselines not stated).
missing.locator: The fix... section, text after the Gemma-3-12B contrast table

missing.what: Induction outcomes for the other Gemma-3 recipes: masked degenerates on ~half of prompts, winsorized on ~a third, raw on 100%.
Median KL of raw ablation is 21–30 across all four Gemma-3 sizes (1b–27b), against 0.04–0.57 for Llama, Qwen and Gemma-2. Raw ablation goes far out of distribution across the Gemma-3 family.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. Inference-time only, so V2 is untested despite the 'abliteration' framing. Feasibility counts (raw 0 feasible on all Gemma-3 sizes) are selection outcomes and are rightly not rows, but they show the raw recipe fails family-wide. No uncertainty estimates; 500-question MMLU slice; induction uses 32 prompts.

versions.untested_parts: The post does not establish that every safety-trained chat model has one direction, or that all other abilities are preserved; it tests selected models, prompt contrasts, and measured capability outcomes.
No weight-space edit or released abliterated model is evaluated; the reported ablation is an inference-time intervention.
No jailbreak suppression mechanism or training against ablation is tested.
The post measures coordinate distribution in standardized class-separation vectors, but does not causally compare affine, cone, or multi-direction refusal representations.
No separate harmfulness-judgment and refusal-decision representation is tested.
No cross-language transfer, base-to-instruct transfer of the refusal direction, or transfer across model variants is established.

The post finds the loud channel in a base checkpoint but says this does not establish identical intervention behavior there; it does not test when refusal training creates a removable refusal direction.
